title: Matryoshka vs Standard SAE: Which Preserves Safety Features Under Scaling?

original_idea.body:
# Matryoshka vs Standard SAE: Which Preserves Safety Features Under Scaling?

**Problem:** Matryoshka SAEs prevent high-level feature absorption, but whether safety-relevant high-level features are better preserved is unverified.

**Direction:** Compare an open Matryoshka SAE against a standard SAE on the same model/layer for persistence/cleanliness of a safety feature across dictionary scales.

**Why it matters:** Relevant to choosing monitoring tooling. Public weights.

**Relevant context:** Bussmann et al. (Alignment Forum); arXiv 2409.14507.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (tooling choice for monitoring) but indirect catastrophic-risk link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Compare two pre-trained SAEs on one feature; no training, guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused architecture comparison on one safety feature; few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public weights, architecture comparison labs won't prioritize; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on public SAEs; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Matryoshka SAEs are new; the safety-feature-preservation comparison may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Matryoshka SAEs exist; the safety-feature-specific comparison may be open.
